sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The serpent stone is a small round piece of glass. The druids used it for divination and healing. Romans called it druid’s glass or ovum anguinum. Pliny wrote that a Vocontian warrior carried one. Emperor Claudius had that warrior executed because Rome feared the stone. Serpents formed the stone in summer at a certain moon phase. They writhed together and secreted a liquid ball into the air. The garter snake shows similar mating behavior. The stone healed bewitchment. A glass of water held the stone after dipping. The cure served sufferers of many kinds. Folklore treasured the stone as medicine long after the druids faded.
